description: We are young computer engineering students.
summary: The idea behind the project is to create a simulator in which people can experience, to some extent, what it is like to live in space by managing a base on Mars. Through an application, participants will be responsible for managing everything necessary to keep the crew alive and the mission operational, including oxygen, water, energy, food, and radiation protection. Throughout the simulation, they will have to make important decisions, solve problems, and learn how to manage limited resources, just as in a real space mission. The objective is to make learning about space more engaging by demonstrating that exploring other planets requires extensive planning, careful management, and responsibility.
details:
AstroBase is an educational simulator in which players take command of a human base on Mars. The objective is to keep the astronauts alive and ensure the base remains operational by managing resources such as oxygen, water, energy, and food. The game operates on Martian days, known as sols. During each turn, players assess the situation, make decisions, and end the day to observe the consequences of their actions. The application features three main tabs: Mission, which presents the objectives and the current status of the base; Crew, which displays the astronauts' conditions; and Journal, which records the events throughout the journey. It also includes a campaign featuring different missions.

The project transforms concepts from science and space engineering into a practical and interactive experience. In addition to teaching players about survival on Mars, it encourages logical reasoning, planning, teamwork, and decision-making skills. Our goal is to inspire young people to develop an interest in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and space exploration.

To develop the simulator, we used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, along with the Three.js library for 3D graphics. The interface was created using HTML and CSS, incorporating icons and visual elements in SVG format. The game runs in web browsers and was designed to operate on standard computers and mobile devices.

One of its main creative features is its visual identity, inspired by Mars and characterized by orange and cyan colors, as well as its mascot, Nico, who was created to make the experience more enjoyable and welcoming. The Journal and the campaign also help develop a narrative throughout the mission.

During the development process, we primarily considered the target audience's age, ease of use, adaptability to different screen sizes, and performance on educational devices. Our aim was to create an accessible, educational, and engaging experience. AI was used in some parts of the project, such as the creation of the simulator, translation and research.
